name: Ratio (Unbalanced) Strangle, 1x2
summary: A short strangle with unequal contract counts on each side - e.g. 1 short call against 2 short puts - to lean the delta and the tail toward the side you believe is safer.

legs.strike_rule: |put delta| 0.10-0.12; put-heavy version shown, invert the ratios for the call-heavy version

max_profit: total net credit x 100 if the underlying settles between the two strikes
max_loss: UNDEFINED on both sides: 2 x $100 per point below the put strike (to zero) and unlimited above the call strike
breakevens: lower = put strike - total credit per share / 2; upper = call strike + total credit per share

greeks.delta: deliberately non-zero, typically +0.05 to +0.15 per unit for the put-heavy version
greeks.gamma: negative and asymmetric - twice as fast on the doubled side
greeks.theta: positive, higher than a balanced strangle for the same strikes

when_to_use: INCLUDED FOR COMPLETENESS ONLY - NOT TRADEABLE AT LEVEL 3. Used when skew makes one side pay far more per unit of delta, or to express a mild directional lean inside a premium-selling program.
entry_rules: BLOCKED: every leg is uncovered; requires Alpaca options level 4.
LEVEL 3 SUBSTITUTE: build it as a quantity-unbalanced iron condor (see slug unbalanced-iron-condor-2x1), which is the same delta and theta shape with defined wings.
If enabled at level 4: IVR >= 40, the doubled side's strike must be >= 1.5 standard deviations away, total naked notional <= 40% of equity.
management_rules: Take profit at 50% of total credit.
Close the doubled side first if its strike delta reaches 0.30.
Never add contracts to the untested side to re-balance delta - that raises gross naked exposure.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: every short leg flat by 15:30 ET on expiration day.
Close any short at extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85; short calls also close before any ex-dividend date while ITM.
Close the whole unit if the underlying closes beyond either short strike.
assignment_risk: Three naked shorts per unit. Put-side assignment delivers 200 shares; call-side assignment creates a 100-share naked short. Both violate the never-be-assigned rule outright.
buying_power: Naked margin on all three contracts, computed per side with the larger side governing; recomputed daily.
liquidity_needs: Liquid ETF chains only; both strikes must be closeable in one MLeg order.
common_mistakes: Believing the extra credit on the doubled side compensates for double the gamma; it does not at the tail.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
